title: Two Ledgers, No Crosstalk
description: The same customer can have several shipments in flight at once, each with its own invoice — make sure paying off one never bleeds into another's numbers.
successCondition: As the same customer, book two shipments and create an invoice for each. Pay invoice A fully (succeeded card) but leave invoice B untouched. GET /api/billing/invoices for that customer shows invoice A as "paid" and invoice B still "open". Querying via `npm run db:psql`: invoice B's row has zero associated payments rows (select count(*) from payments where invoice_id = '<B id>' is 0), and both invoices' customer_id columns correctly match the same customer while their shipment_id columns differ.
hints: Each Payment row's invoiceId scopes it to exactly one invoice — there's no shared "customer wallet" table that payments write to instead.
GET /api/billing/invoices lists every invoice for the caller — filter the response by shipmentId to tell A and B apart.
